oncall-bot: PAGER: GPU pool surge detected in us-west-2 -> sustained queue growth, 429s rising, customer-facing latency increases. Incident created: INC-2026-3951236789 :rotating_light:

jamie_ops: seeing continuous 429s on hotpath pool A-uw2, queue length up from ~120 -> 2.4k in 6m. autoscaler not adding GPUs.

sara_sre: looking. early signs that tokenbucket refill for tier=gold is capped incorrectly (0.5 r/s) vs expected 5 r/s after last deploy.

leo_infra: confirmed, autoscaler heartbeat healthy but pool can't accept new tasks because token gating rejects with 429 before scheduling. stack shows: 
```
ERROR: request_rejected: rate_limiter(tier=gold) token_acquire failed (0 tokens)
queue: 2403
active_gpus: 18/18
pending_scale: 0
autoscaler_state: min_reached
```

jamie_ops: why pending_scale = 0? autoscaler config min=18 max=36, should spawn but policy says "no_scale_if_rate_limited" (was added as safety).

marta_prod: that policy was part of last week's emergency change to avoid runaway scale on noisy tenants. maybe too conservative now. customers reporting higher latency and some 429s from Redwood API.

carlos_support: field reports: mobile search retries spiking, a few enterprise customers seeing high error rates. Support ticket count +3 in last 10m.

jamie_ops: mitigation options: 1) temporarily bump tokenbucket refill for tier=gold to 6 r/s 2) disable "no_scale_if_rate_limited" flag so autoscaler can act 3) increase pool max to 48 4) route traffic of heavy tenants to coldpool. Thoughts?

sara_sre: priority order: 2 then 1. Let autoscaler do its job first (fast), then tune tokenbucket to avoid immediate rejections. Changing refill will let more requests through but if autoscaler still blocked we just increase load on gpus.

leo_infra: I can flip the flag now. Doing it via infra-admin: 
```bash
# flip safety flag (one-line risk acknowledged)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $INFRATOKEN" https://infra.redwood.internal/api/v1/autoscaler/configs/flags -d '{"no_scale_if_rate_limited": false}'
```

jamie_ops: go ahead. ping here when done. I'm preparing runbook steps for rollback.

(oncall-bot): action: infra-change-request created CR-3951236789 by leo_infra.

leo_infra: flipped flag. status: success. autoscaler observed new work queued. pending_scale -> 8 now.

sara_sre: nice. I'll watch tokenbucket meter; we still have a backlog so we'll likely see gpus spin up.

10m later...

leo_infra: GPUs spun from 18 -> 28 over 9m; queue down to 700. 429s dropped 80%. dashboards: https://console.redwood/infradash/incidents/3951236789 :white_check_mark:

marta_prod: pushing customer comms draft to #marketing for notification. need ETA to healthy baseline for support message?

carlos_support: tell customers we're mitigating, expected 30-60m for full normalization, provide workaround: reduce concurrency or retry with backoff.

jamie_ops: follow-up: we still saw some 429 spikes at seconds resolution. root cause path: safety flag prevented autoscaler from scaling under the assumption token gating meant overload; combined with a mis-deployed tokenbucket refill param (0.5 r/s) created a choke point. 

sara_sre: propose post-incident actions: 
- revert last-week emergency change that added blanket "no_scale_if_rate_limited" (clamp to per-tenant exceptions)
- add a canary check in deploy pipeline to validate tokenbucket refill values against expected thresholds for each tier
- add metric: tokenbucket_block_rate per pool-level to trigger auto-override (allow scaling after X blocked requests in Ys)
- update runbook step 3 to include immediate autoscaler override instructions

leo_infra: agree. I'll open follow-up RFC for autoscaler-safety behavior RFC-3951236789-RFC.

marta_prod: note from ops: affected customers list: #enterprise-acct-42, #acme-marketing, #qantas-ml. Support escalation created.

carlos_support: I've sent initial notice to affected customer AMs and scheduled a 1:1 for tomorrow.

jamie_ops: tagging for handoff: night oncall @leo_infra will own monitoring until fully normalized. leave patch open, don't rollback the flag until we have tokenbucket fixes + canary.

leo_infra: taking handoff. I'll put a short-term mitigation: increase gold refill to 6 r/s during night window and set an alert to rollback if error rate increases. Executing now.

(oncall-bot): action: alert suppressed for GPU-queue-spike, escalation paused.

leo_infra: refill bumped. command: 
```json
{"tier":"gold","refill_rps":6}
```
applied via config api.

sara_sre: monitors look stable. queue ~230 -> plan: keep refill 6 r/s and safety flag false overnight. Tomorrow we'll run a controlled deploy with canary checks.

jamie_ops: incident severity: Sev2 -> customer impact but degraded not complete outage. Postmortem assigned to sara_sre + leo_infra. ETA preliminary postmortem within 48h.

marta_prod: I'll coordinate customer comms and postmortem summary for execs.

carlos_support: logging note: captured sample request ids and 429 payloads, attaching to INC ticket.

jamie_ops: final note before handoff: action-items: 
- leia: (sara_sre) create deploy gate for tokenbucket defaults (P0)
- leo_infra: write RFC for selective safety gating and autoscaler override (P1)
- marta_prod + carlos_support: customer notifications and follow-ups (P1)
- jamie_ops: coordinate postmortem and link dashboards (P1)

leo_infra: acknowledging handoff. monitoring and escalation channel open. ping me if errors > 5% in next 2 hours.

(oncall-bot): incident INC-2026-3951236789 status -> monitoring.

jamie_ops: thanks team. :party_parrot:
